senses.gloss: marked by extreme intensity of emotions or convictions; inclined to react violently; fervid
senses.learner: full of very strong feelings or beliefs, or quick to react with great force.

senses.gloss: acting with or marked by or resulting from great force or energy or emotional intensity
senses.learner: acting with, showing, or caused by great force, great energy, or very strong feeling.
examples: accompanied by a violent yawn.
The storm brought violent winds that tore the roof off the barn.

senses.gloss: effected by force or injury rather than natural causes
senses.learner: caused by force or injury, not by natural causes.
examples: He died a violent death at the hands of robbers.

senses.gloss: characterized by violence or bloodshed
(of colors or sounds) intensely vivid or loud
senses.learner: of colours or sounds: very bright and strong, or very loud.
examples: She wore a dress of a violent pink that hurt the eyes.

connotation.why: may judge a colour or sound as too harsh, against 'vivid'

senses.gloss: low or inferior in station or quality
marked by meekness or modesty; not arrogant or prideful
of low birth or station (‘base’ is archaic in this sense)

senses.gloss: used of unskilled work (especially domestic work)

examples: She took humble jobs, washing floors and scrubbing pots.

connotation.why: softer than 'menial' for the same work

senses.gloss: directly relevant to a matter especially a law case
senses.learner: directly connected to the matter being dealt with, especially a case in a court of law.
examples: The judge ruled that the letter was material to the case.

senses.gloss: concerned with worldly rather than spiritual interests
senses.learner: having to do with the things of this world rather than with matters of the spirit.
examples: The monks turned away from material things to seek God.

senses.gloss: having material or physical form or substance
senses.learner: having a real physical form or substance.

senses.gloss: concerned with or affecting physical as distinct from intellectual or psychological well-being
senses.learner: having to do with or affecting the well-being of the body, as opposed to the well-being of the mind or feelings.
examples: Food and shelter are our most basic material needs.

senses.gloss: derived from or composed of matter
senses.learner: made of, or coming from, matter.
examples: Stars and planets are part of the material universe.

senses.gloss: having substance or capable of being treated as fact; not imaginary
senses.learner: having real substance, or able to be treated as fact; not imagined.
examples: The danger was material, not something he had dreamed up.

senses.gloss: (usually followed by ‘to’) naturally disposed toward
having made preparations
senses.learner: having got everything ready; prepared.
examples: The army stood disposed for the attack, every man in his place.

senses.gloss: limit the inheritance of property to a specific class of heirs
senses.learner: to limit who can inherit a piece of property to one particular group of heirs.
examples: There is no knowing how estates will go when once they come to be entailed.
Your father's estate is entailed on Mr. Collins, I think?

senses.gloss: impose, involve, or imply as a necessary accompaniment or result
senses.learner: to force, include, or suggest something as a part or result that must come along with it.
examples: The new job will entail a lot of travel.

senses.gloss: have as a logical consequence
senses.learner: to have something as a result that follows by logic.
examples: Being a square entails having four sides.

senses.gloss: yet to be or coming
senses.learner: still to come or still to exist; not here yet.
examples: his prospects of future wealth were exceedingly fair.
I singled you out as the companion of my future life.

senses.gloss: effective in or looking toward the future
senses.learner: taking effect later on, or looking ahead to the time to come.
examples: The new rule applies only to future contracts, not to those already signed.

senses.gloss: a verb tense or other formation referring to events or states that have not yet happened
senses.learner: used of a verb tense or other form that talks about things that have not happened yet.
examples: In 'she will sing', the verb is in the future tense.

senses.gloss: (of elected officers) elected but not yet serving
senses.learner: of a person chosen in an election: chosen but not yet in office.
examples: The future mayor, elected last week, will take office in January.

senses.gloss: dignified and somber in manner or character and committed to keeping promises
senses.learner: serious, dignified and solemn in manner or character, and careful to keep your promises.
examples: His air was grave and stately, and his manners were very formal.
her husband looked impenetrably grave

senses.gloss: of great gravity or crucial import; requiring serious thought
senses.learner: very serious or very important, and needing careful thought.
examples: She had to make a grave choice between her family and her work.

senses.gloss: causing fear or anxiety by threatening great harm

senses.gloss: guess correctly; solve by guessing

Elizabeth, immediately recognizing the livery, guessed what it meant

senses.gloss: expect, believe, or suppose
judge tentatively or form an estimate of (quantities or time)

senses.gloss: a feeling of righteous anger
senses.learner: anger that you feel because you believe something is wrong or unfair.
examples: Elizabeth made no answer, and walked on, her heart swelling with indignation.
heard it in silent indignation.

senses.gloss: the trait of being uncommunicative; not volunteering anything more than necessary

senses.gloss: formality and propriety of manner
something kept back or saved for future use or a special purpose
senses.learner: something kept back or saved so that it can be used later or for a special purpose

senses.gloss: a district that is reserved for particular purpose
senses.learner: an area of land that is kept for a particular purpose

senses.gloss: armed forces that are not on active duty but can be called in an emergency
senses.learner: soldiers who are not on active duty but can be called to serve in an emergency

senses.gloss: an athlete who plays only when a starter on the team is replaced
senses.learner: a player who plays only when one of the team's starting players is taken off

senses.gloss: (medicine) potential capacity to respond in order to maintain vital functions
senses.learner: in medicine, the ability the body has in store to respond so that it can keep its life-supporting functions working
examples: Older patients have less heart reserve, so a long operation is riskier for them.
